\chapter{\texorpdfstring{scriptura's blocks}{scriptura's blocks}}
\label{chap:scriptura-blocks}

\textbf{Purpose:} The one rule on what scriptura's SWAR memory scans may be handed, and why it settles the over-read question.

\textbf{Scope:} \texttt{scriptura\_\allowbreak{}compare}, \texttt{scriptura\_\allowbreak{}length}, \texttt{scriptura\_\allowbreak{}find}, \texttt{scriptura\_\allowbreak{}copy}, \texttt{scriptura\_\allowbreak{}fill} (M17 of \hyperref[chap:engine-table]{engine\_\allowbreak{}table.md}).

Ruled by Doug, 23 September: “never pass unaligned memory to this, ever”; “the solution is to always nul term memory blocks you hand it”.

\begin{itemize}
\item Every block handed to the scriptura word scans is 8-byte aligned and NUL-terminated. A string literal is not guaranteed aligned: copy it into an aligned block first.
\item Used this way, \texttt{scriptura\_\allowbreak{}compare(a, b, length of b + 1)} returns strcmp's sign. The bytes read past a short block's NUL never change the result (the first differing lane decides it, bitwise). An aligned word never crosses a page.
\item The over-read question is settled by this rule and is not reopened.
\end{itemize}
